newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended marginally firmer on Wednesday on the back of a bullish gold price and a steady rand, dealers said.
Industrials took a knock amid profit-taking.
"Overall it has been a mixed day. Golds have been pretty interesting while industrials have drifted marginally," one dealer said.
Gold traded around the $353 level for most of Wednesday, while the rand hovered around the 4.43 level.
"The gold sentiment has improved of late and we are seeing a bit of a scare on some negative industrial news. Some guys are taking a bit of profit," another dealer said.
Worse-than-expected results on Tuesday from synthetic fuel company Sasol in particular was cited as a reason for the fall in the industrial index on the day.
"I don't think we need to panic but I think another set of poor results from a big industrial stock could cause a little bit of concern," one dealer added.
The industrial index ended down 46.7 points at 8,378.8.
The overall index climbed 2.9 points 7,205.7, while gold index gained 4.9 to 1,543.4.
They said volumes of about 821 million rand had been traded towards close around 1425 GMT.
Traders said there heavy volume had traded in Sasol on the day. The counter ended down 150 cents at 50.00 rand on turnover of nearly two million shares.

"The volume leader has been Sasol with some foreigners seeming to like it at around 50 rand. Our Thursday market will probably be firmer if the financial statistics coming out tommorrow are good," a dealer commented.

January trade data is scheduled for release at 0800 GMT on Thursday and after the trade data, fourth quarter gross domestic product, January inflation, money supply and credit extension growth data will be released.
Dealers said among Wednesday's market movers had been Sappi, which added 90 cents to 36.25 rand, De Beers which jumped 250 cents to 158.50 and South African Breweries which shed 250 cents to 138.00.
Near-dated gold share futures ended firm, but off their highs as bullion staged a marginal recovery and industrial contracts retreated on a weaker rand and long bonds.
The March gold contract was at 1,087/95 from 1,095, the industrial contract at 8,085/905 from 8,216 and the all-share contract at 6,555/70 from 6,601.
